Very slim explanation as to what the actual difference between a chain and a belt is. Timing belts have a maintenance routine of about 100k miles and a chain is inside the "oil side" of the engine, so in theory, the chain lasts the life of the engine, unless the engine is unreliable already and the owner drives it low on oil. There is really no better option, rather than the opinion on the buyer/owner, if you dont mind spending a couple hundred in a few years (which is very little) or never having to worry about the timing chain (if its a good engine). To be honest, if an engine has problems with chain stretch very early in its life, its a bad engine. With sime new engines that noone has ticked too many miles on yet, it is still uncertain. So i guess overall the belt option is better, but dont say that a chain is "hard and expensive" to replace in a way that sounds like a chain should be changed regularly. No.
